rubric.result: The objective promises two things and the diff produces both. (a) 'the cabin presses the promotion with the key it was handed': EpicPromotionRoute.promoting() demands GateKey.HEADER before anything is asked (`if (!key.holds(request.get(GateKey.HEADER)))`), then reads the checkout out of `held().conversation`, asks PromoteEpic.execute with a PromoteEpicParams built from root+repository, and answers 200 {status, milestone, issues, promoted} through #wireIssueOf. (b) 'is refused with {code, detail} when there is nothing to authorise': EpicPromotionRefusal projects the four no-issue rungs to a 400 {code:'no-epic-issues', detail:'the milestone holds no issue yet: the groom has to run first'}, and the two other refusals of the vocabulary (403 gate-not-from-the-page, 400 no-coordinating-session) are produced too. The RECORD line the task's prose adds is written by #recordOf on the success path only. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The TDD line names it('a post with no gate key is refused and the promotion is never asked') and fixes three things: 403, the literal body, and the PromoteEpic double untouched. The test asserts exactly those: `expect(response.status).toBe(403)`, `toEqual({code:'gate-not-from-the-page', detail:'gate 2 answers only a request carrying the key the page was given'})` and `expect(promote.asked).toEqual([])`. Same input, same expected value. I read it the way this task was asked to be read: could it fail for the reason its name gives? Yes. `RunningApi.posting(port)` is called with its default `{}` headers, so the request carries no x-gate-key at all (unlike the sibling, where every request set the headers by hand). With the `key.holds` guard deleted the handler falls through to `held.held()` — Mother.live() holds one — and then to `promote.execute`, where PromoteEpicSpy.neverAsked() throws; express 5 forwards the rejected handler promise to its error handler, so the answer is a 500 and both the status assertion and `promote.asked` fall. Its boundary pair, it('the same post carrying the key answers the issues and which numbers it moved'), is present and asserts the 200 wire body including `promoted: [1]`.

Compared name by name against the Contract block. EpicPromotionOutcome: the four members with the literal values ACCEPTED 'accepted', NOT_FROM_THE_PAGE 'gate-not-from-the-page', NO_COORDINATING_SESSION 'no-coordinating-session', NO_EPIC_ISSUES 'no-epic-issues', frozen and `as const`. EpicPromotionRoute: PATH '/epic-promotion', METHOD 'POST', RECORD 'gate 2 promotion'. `static promoting(held: CoordinatingSessions, promote: PromoteEpic, key: GateKey, stderr: (line: string) => void): RequestHandler` — same parameter names, same order, same return type. `static refuseOtherMethods(request: Request, response: Response): void` — same, and it sets `Allow: POST` from METHOD. The prose's further demands also hold: no body and no JsonBody middleware, the checkout out of held().conversation, the Projection over the four rungs no-spec/draft/awaiting-publication/groomable to the single no-epic-issues, and every other rung a 200 {status, milestone, issues, promoted}. The refusal-codes.test.ts change is the one line the vocabulary needs.

Row by row, the rows this diff bears on: D-22 (the gates are the human's; no endpoint a session can call, an attempt refused with an explicit code) — implemented as written, the key is demanded before anything is asked and the refusal is the explicit code gate-not-from-the-page, 403. D-6 (gate 2 is an act of the app with its own yardstick) — the promotion is a POST the program answers for. D-10 (everything new under backend/ is TypeScript) — both new files are .ts. D-13 (no phase is stored) — the route stores nothing; the state comes back from PromoteEpic, which derives it from evidence. D-7 (nothing writes to a pull request, no merge button) — the diff touches neither. D-11, D-23, D-25 and the rest have no subject in these three files, and no row is reopened.

Exemplars: `backend/src/infrastructure/spec-freeze-route.ts` and the sibling `epic-groom-route.ts` are matched line for line in shape — Answer/Refusal from http.ts, a Projection of refusals, the gate-key guard first, the PlanFailure -> PlanCollapse catch, #wireIssueOf, refuseOtherMethods with Allow. `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/epic-groom-route.test.ts` is matched by the new test: a real listening server on port 0, a real fetch client, a Mother with named scenarios, an afterEach that closes every server. ct's yardstick, document by document. style.md: no comment or docstring anywhere in either file; every identifier, test name and diagnostic in English (the only non-English tokens are `status:ready` and `status:backlog`, which CLAUDE.md pins as the loop's contract vocabulary); no free function at module level — everything hangs off EpicPromotionOutcome, EpicPromotionRefusal, EpicPromotionRoute, and in the test off PromoteEpicSpy, Keys, LiveSessionsDouble, Mother and RunningApi. architecture.md: 'One controller per endpoint' — the route, its closed vocabulary of outcomes and its refusal projection travel in one new module, and the wiring is task 9's. Dependencies point inwards only (infrastructure -> application -> domain). boundaries.md: 'The code of an answer is declared explicitly, beside its detail, and never derived from an exception's class name' — both details are named constants beside their codes; the PlanFailure catch goes through PlanCollapse, which already declares `epic-issue-not-promoted` for the EpicIssueNotPromoted that GhEpicIssues.promote throws (start-plan-route.ts:345), so the implementer's first design call is sound and the branch is reachable rather than defensive. decisions.md: the implementer's second design call is right — the four-rung partition is declared once, in EpicPromotionRefusal.#BY_STATE, and appliesTo() reads it back with .members(), so the antipattern 'the same partition of a closed vocabulary declared in more than one place' is avoided (the sibling does declare its three rungs twice, in GroomEpic.REFUSED and in EpicGroomRefusal.#BY_STATE; this diff does not repeat that). defects.md, its four rules: (1) closed vocabulary — EpicPromotionOutcome is frozen and closed, the state travels as EpicGroomStateValue and no value is classified by a loose string or a boolean; the one thing to weigh is that the success path is 'not one of the four rungs -> 200', which is a binary partition rather than an exhaustive dispatch, so a seventh EpicGroomState member would pass through as a 200 — but that is exactly what the task prescribes ('every other rung is a 200') and exactly what the neighbour's grooming() handler does, so it is the plan's shape, not the implementer's; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — none: #wireIssueOf builds a typed WireIssue one step before Answer.send, which is the serialization boundary itself, and nothing downstream decides anything with it; (3) two fields that have to agree, sentinel for an absence — none: `milestone: string | null` carries the absence in the type, `promoted` is a list whose emptiness is the fact and no flag repeats it, and the 'no issue' word in the record line is rendering, not a stored sentinel; (4) an error named for where it happens — no new error is declared, and the refusal code no-epic-issues names what happens. simplicity.md is the one place I have something to cite, and it is small: Mother.backlogIssue() in the new test file is never called (reported below, low). Delivery: this is a new file plus one import in a vocabulary guard, no signature changed and no call site left on an old path, so no document of either yardstick has an expand-contract shape to demand here. Both named skills are the epic's (`backend-engineering:backend-best-practices`, `frontend-engineering:frontend-best-practices`); I read the diff against ct's eight documents and the repo's CLAUDE.md, which is where the rules that bear on it are written.

One pre-existing test file is touched, backend/__tests__/infrastructure/refusal-codes.test.ts, and the diff has no `-` line anywhere (403 insertions, 0 deletions). The two added lines widen what the guard measures: EpicPromotionOutcome's members now enter RequestVocabularies.codes(), so the three assertions run over a larger set. SharedOnPurposeAcrossRequestVocabularies.CODES was deliberately not widened — I checked that it did not need to be: gate-not-from-the-page and no-coordinating-session already appear twice and Repeats.within reports distinct codes, and no-epic-issues is unique — so the repeat guard was not relaxed to let the new vocabulary in. Nothing stopped asserting.

The behaviour the objective promises lives in backend/src/infrastructure/epic-promotion-route.ts: the 403 and its detail, the 400 no-epic-issues built by EpicPromotionRefusal from the Projection, the 400 no-coordinating-session, the 200 body built by #wireIssueOf, the RECORD line built by #recordOf. Each test reaches all of it through a real express server and a real fetch, so no assertion is on the scaffolding's own product. The only double is PromoteEpic, which is the seam conventions/testing.md prescribes for a controller ('the use case, by construction'), and the promotion itself is measured at its own layer in backend/__tests__/application/promote-epic.test.ts. Revert the production file and every one of the six tests fails.

The diff writes only inside the three paths **Files:** names, and inside them only what the task's sentences ask for: the route with its vocabulary and its refusal projection (the prose names EpicPromotionRefusal by name), the six tests the **Tests:** line lists and nothing else, and the one import plus one spread in refusal-codes.test.ts. Nothing in `### Out of scope` is touched: no ct-groom.mjs, no groom.js, no --reconcile or Project v2, no dispatcher or gate 1 change, no write to a pull request, no repository column. The wiring into api-server.ts and ct-api.ts, which a diff serving the slice's end might have been tempted to add, is left to task 9 where the plan puts it. No hunk of the plan file appears in the diff, so there is no amendment to rule on, and the implementer's report says none was needed. The only dead weight I found is a test helper with no caller, reported under patrones rather than duplicated here.

Six new tests, all in epic-promotion-route.test.ts. Deterministic: the key is minted from Keys.RANDOM = Buffer.alloc(size, 7), a fixed seed rather than crypto randomness, and the expected value Keys.MINTED is derived from GateKey.BYTES rather than pasted; no clock, no date, no network beyond 127.0.0.1, no sleep, and the server binds port 0 so nothing depends on a fixed port. Isolated: each test builds its own CoordinatingSessions and its own spy, the only shared mutable state is RunningApi.#started, which the afterEach splices and closes, and no test needs another to have run first. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on the status, headers and literal body that came back over HTTP from the production handler, or on the line the production #recordOf handed to the stderr sink — none is on a double's call count or on a constant the test defined (the `promote.asked` assertions are the refusal-never-reached-the-use-case check conventions/testing.md requires, not the subject of the assertion). I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and read the diff against it; the one thing it flags — 'One thing. "and" in name? Split it.' — falls on two names the plan itself dictated verbatim in its **TDD:** and **Tests:** lines, so it is not the implementer's to answer for, and in both cases the two clauses are facets of one behaviour (a refusal and its absence of side effect). Nothing here rises even to a low.

findings.what: Mother.backlogIssue() is defined in the new test file and never called by any of the six tests — it is a leftover of the sibling's mother (where it is used twice, and where it is numbered 2 against readyIssue's 1; here both scenarios carry number 1, which is what shows it was copied rather than needed). conventions/simplicity.md asks which call breaks without it: none does, and with it goes the only use of the PlanIssueStatus.BACKLOG import in this file. No behaviour is affected, which is why this is a low.
